reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes StrongBlock node participation as a way to earn rewards and passive income, directing viewers to create a node. The promoted flow requires a non-refundable, non-returnable contribution of 10 STRONG and may involve recurring fees, tying the income claim to a financial commitment.

citations.quote: Log on to StrongBlock Click create a node Name your node and give it a description
Earn passive income with strongblock nodes.

opening.argument: Judge, the node-creation screen visibly discloses that the required contribution is non-refundable and non-returnable [F0024]. The node dashboard also warns that failure to pay a monthly fee may result in automatic removal [F0035]. Those are material limitations to the opportunity being shown, not a presentation that hides every cost or condition. The title promises passive income [TITLE_0001], but the visible terms give viewers reason to assess that promise cautiously. Treating the video as an operational demonstration with disclosed risks is a more precise reading than treating the income language alone as proof of deception.

citations.quote: Earn passive income with strongblock nodes.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution is right that the narration directs viewers through node creation [ASR_0001] and that participation requires a non-refundable contribution [F0024]. But those points do not establish concealment: the contribution condition appears on the creation screen itself. The dashboard likewise displays the monthly-fee consequence [F0035]. A paid, risky service can be demonstrated and promoted without this record establishing that its terms were withheld or its returns guaranteed.

citations.quote: Log on to StrongBlock Click create a node Name your node and give it a description

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Visible terms do not turn this into a risk warning. The video instructs viewers to create a node [ASR_0001], shows the required non-refundable contribution [F0024], displays rewards alongside nodes [F0035], and ends with a passive-income appeal [F0053]. The defense identifies disclosed costs, but those costs are precisely what tie the promoted returns to paid node participation. Nothing cited shows the creator cautioning viewers against the income claim.

citations.quote: Log on to StrongBlock Click create a node Name your node and give it a description

opening.argument: Judge, much of the video follows an interface task: log on, click to create a node, then supply its name and description [ASR_0001]. The corresponding screen shows protocol choices and fields for those entries [F0024]; a later screen shows a node dashboard [F0035]. These are concrete steps and screens a viewer could use to understand how the tool operates. The passive-income title [TITLE_0001] supplies the topic, but it does not erase the instructional content or establish that the creator obtained a contribution from anyone. Classify the observed material by what it substantially shows: a node-setup demonstration.

citations.quote: Log on to StrongBlock Click create a node Name your node and give it a description
Earn passive income with strongblock nodes.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution identifies a required contribution on the form [F0024], but showing a requirement during a walkthrough is also what an informative tutorial would do. Its cited instruction is limited to navigating the site and filling out node details [ASR_0001]. The dashboard's displayed rewards [F0035] illustrate the interface; they do not prove that the presenter received those amounts or that a viewer will receive them. The record supports an instructional reading even though the presentation is enthusiastic.

citations.quote: Log on to StrongBlock Click create a node Name your node and give it a description

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The walkthrough is not neutral in context. It tells viewers how to create the node [ASR_0001], the creation screen requires a non-refundable contribution [F0024], and the video explicitly tells viewers they can earn passive income [ASR_0001]. The dashboard's reward display [F0035] reinforces that pitch. No completed contribution or realized payout is needed to identify the promoted paid-node returns mechanism.

citations.quote: Log on to StrongBlock Click create a node Name your node and give it a description Earn rewards here Earn passive income from anywhere while sipping a Pierre Covarde

opening.argument: Judge, this is a presentation of an identifiable node service, with a creation form that states its required contribution [F0024] and a dashboard that shows nodes, rewards and a monthly-fee condition [F0035]. Those screens support a paid-service reading. The narration's invitation to create a node and earn rewards [ASR_0001] is promotional, but the supplied material does not show a promised fixed return, a request for the viewer's credentials, or a completed payment or payout. The question is not whether the service is safe; it is whether these screens and this pitch establish more than promotion of a risky paid service.

citations.quote: Log on to StrongBlock Click create a node Name your node and give it a description Earn rewards here

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution's strongest point is the 10 STRONG requirement on the creation screen [F0024]. That establishes an entry cost, not that the money was taken deceptively or that any particular return was guaranteed. The title speaks broadly of passive income [TITLE_0001], while the dashboard displays reward figures alongside a fee warning [F0035]. Neither cited screen shows a completed transaction or verifies what a participant ultimately receives. Promotion of a paid service should not be treated as proof of a fraudulent payout.

citations.quote: Earn passive income with strongblock nodes.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A guaranteed rate or completed payment is not the relevant threshold. The video directs viewers to create a node and says they can earn rewards and passive income [ASR_0001]. The form requires a non-refundable contribution to participate [F0024], and the dashboard links nodes to displayed rewards while noting a recurring fee [F0035]. Calling that ordinary commerce leaves the video's central paid-entry-for-node-returns pitch unanswered.
